Criteria for the lighting of Federally financed highway projects is established in "An Informational Guide for Roadway Lighting" published by the American Association of State Highway Officials. Non-Federal projects often use the AASHO recommendations as minimum standards. The currently recommended level of illumination for freeways is 0.6 to 0.8 footcandle at the time of lowest effective light output, or approximately 1.0 footcandle, minimum, at the time of installation. Studies are now being conducted which might lead to an increase in this recommended level of illumination. There is a proposed toll plaza for the Expressway located between Allen Avenue and Randolph Street which can be expected to be lighted to a considerably higher level of illumination, with possibly to 5.0 footcandles maintained. If adaptation, or transition, lighting is used adjacent to the toll plaza, it can be expected that the major portion of the expressway within the project boundary will be lighted to a level greater than AASHO recommendation.
To summarize, the lighting of the Downtown Expressway could have a detrimental effect on the urban renewal project area unless control is exercised over the lighting of the Downtown Expressway. Maximum allowable levels of illumination resulting from the lighting of the Expressway should be established and the lighting designed to within the limits of that criteria. Lighting equipment should be selected that would not impose glare conditions upon the project. Considering the present state of the art of outdoor lighting, it appears feasible to light the Expressway in a manner that would not be detrimental to the project provided that the lighting design gives adequate consideration to the impact of the lighting system upon the adjacent areas.
